note: Builder data of tools/content/modules/economy.mjs: the seven resources, the energy system (Provisions) and the Stored Essence bar, the building names, the state category names, the regional economic identity, the regional spirits and the Golden Court's treasury. Engine keys never change; names change through localisation. Every name, number and text here is proposed by the economy spec. The master plan's P5 sentence ('charcoal and coal') is read as the economy spec reads it: Provisions fed by Grain and Stored Essence (text sweep spec, glossary entries energy and fuel).

resources.name: Essence
resources.role: Raw magic from wellsprings, elder groves, ley-stones and the vents of the Dead Lands
resources.warfareUse: Wards and other magical equipment; the Stored Essence bar

resources.name: Gold
resources.warfareUse: Elven arms, knightly plate and flagship fittings

resources.name: Grain
resources.role: Grain, fish and fodder; it feeds the Provisions of every workshop, forge and yard
resources.warfareUse: Never in a cost; it becomes Provisions

energy.meaning: The engine's energy system is the Provisions of Erdae: bread, fodder and firewood that keep the hands of every workshop, forge and yard at work. Grain extracted in a realm is eaten as Provisions (RESOURCE_TO_ENERGY_COEFFICIENT per unit) on top of a small base the hearths always supply (BASE_COUNTRY_ENERGY_PRODUCTION). The engine's fuel bar is Stored Essence: present, never spent, because every equipment burns 0 fuel (warfare spec).

effects.workshops: A realm short of Provisions loses output in each Guild Workshop and builds more slowly (the alert names both).
effects.armouries: Each Armoury makes less and the Output modifier of the forges falls by the same share.
effects.shipwrights: Each Shipwright makes less and the Output modifier of the yards falls by the same share.

model.note: Design model, assumed from the comments of the installed defines (to be measured in the Linux run with the console command energy_ratio and the top bar tooltip): the demand of one building is min(ENERGY_COST_CAP, BASE_ENERGY_COST + ENERGY_SCALING_COST_BY_FACTORY_COUNT x all buildings) and the supply is BASE_COUNTRY_ENERGY_PRODUCTION + RESOURCE_TO_ENERGY_COEFFICIENT x Grain used.

texticons.name: energy_consumption_texticon
texticons.means: Grain eaten as Provisions (an ear of grain)

texticons.name: power_balance_texticon
texticons.means: Balance of Provisions (a pair of scales)

buildings.name: Road
buildings.desc: Roads and bridges let hosts march faster, carry more supplies up from the depots and let mines and quarries yield more.

buildings.name: Armoury
buildings.desc: Forges and benches where smiths and armourers turn out arms and gear for the host. A slot can be turned back into a guild workshop when the realm has need.

buildings.name: Guild Workshop
buildings.desc: Guild craftsmen raise new buildings and make wares for the folk and for trade. A slot can be turned into an armoury when the realm has need.

buildings.name: Shipwright
buildings.desc: Slips and sheds where ships are built and mended for the fleet.

buildings.name: Harbour
buildings.desc: Quays and sea-walls from which fleets sail and are mended. A harbour opens the sea road to cargo and trade, and each level lets more supplies pass.

buildings.name: Eyrie
buildings.desc: Roosts and stables for the winged hosts of the realm. None stand at the start; they are raised once a realm holds dragons.

buildings.name: Depot
buildings.desc: A depot is a storehouse on a high road, away from the cities, where the host may draw its supplies.

buildings.name: High Road
buildings.desc: High roads join the depots, so that supplies may be drawn from far beyond the capital.

buildings.name: Stone Fort
buildings.desc: Each level of a stone fort lowers an attacker's strength in battle by $VALUE|+%0$. Attacks from several sides blunt a fort's worth.

buildings.name: Sea Fort
buildings.desc: Each level of a sea fort lowers an attacker's strength by $VALUE|+%0$ when the enemy lands from the sea.

buildings.name: Fortress Network
buildings.desc: Great forts, walls and signal towers that stand together as one defence, built to turn back an enemy and to hold the key lands.

buildings.name: Scorpion Towers
buildings.desc: Tall towers where bolt-throwers command the sky. They shield the state from raiders on the wing and shoot at those who dive on it.

buildings.name: Beacon Tower
buildings.desc:
Watch fires and signal horns tell us what moves in the nearby states.
A higher tower in a state carries the warning further.
Watchers on the towers also give early word of winged raiders, so our own riders can meet them.
They spot hostile fleets at sea as well.

buildings.name: Victualling Yard
buildings.desc:
A victualling yard lets our fleets take on stores in this harbour as well as in their home ports, which carries their reach further.
It can only be raised in a coastal province that has a harbour of at least level 8.

buildings.name: Admiralty
buildings.desc:
An admiralty lets us seat an admiral to strengthen the fleets that sail within its reach.

Up to $MAXNUM|H$ admiralties can have an admiral seated at one time.
   Seated now: $CURRNUM|H$

An admiralty can only be raised in a coastal province that has a harbour of at least level 8.

buildings.name: Granary
buildings.desc: Deep granaries and well-kept bakehouses mean our workshops, forges and yards eat less of the realm's Provisions, however busy the year.

buildings.name: Mine and Quarry Roads
buildings.desc: Cart-ways cut to the pits and quarries let more ore and stone come out of the ground and reach the forges.

buildings.name: Essence Still
buildings.desc: A still draws Stored Essence from the raw essence of the state. No art of Erdae raises one.

buildings.name: Essence Vault
buildings.desc: A warded vault with room for more Stored Essence. No art of Erdae raises one.

buildings.name: Ritual Ground
buildings.desc: A ring of stones kept for the rarest rites. None stand in Erdae.

buildings.name: Great Engine
buildings.desc: A siege engine of a size no wright of Erdae has built.

buildings.name: Deep Crucible
buildings.desc: A sealed crucible for the deepest rites. None are raised.

buildings.name: Cold Crucible
buildings.desc: A sealed crucible of a colder kind. None are raised.

buildings.name: Hearth Crucible
buildings.desc: A sealed crucible meant for the hearths of the folk. None are raised.

buildings.name: Deep Circle
buildings.desc: A circle of stones where scholars work the Deep Rites.

buildings.name: Roost Circle
buildings.desc: A circle of stones where scholars work the Sky Rites.

buildings.name: Tide Circle
buildings.desc: A circle of stones on the shore where scholars work the Tide Rites.

buildings.name: Warding Circle
buildings.desc: A circle of stones where scholars work the War Rites.

buildings.name: Mill Weir
buildings.desc: A weir across a river to turn mills and feed the channels. None are raised.

buildings.name: Mountain Weir
buildings.desc: A weir in a mountain gorge. None are raised.

buildings.name: Cataract Weir
buildings.desc: A great weir above a cataract. None are raised.

buildings.name: Cut Locks
buildings.desc: The locks of a sea-cut. None are raised.

buildings.name: Neck Locks
buildings.desc: The locks of a cut through a neck of land. None are raised.

interimLandmark.name: Standing Monument
interimLandmark.desc: A monument that stands in no state until Erdae's own landmarks, such as the Golden Court and the gate at Kingson, are raised.

regions.name: Middle Lands
regions.identity: The richest heartland: workshops, lake harbours, high roads

regions.name: Cold Lands
regions.identity: Iron and furs; hard winters; the largest and least developed land

regions.name: Lands of the Sun
regions.identity: Sun-blessed fields of the Sunhot elves

regional.name: The Great Lake Markets
regional.desc: Ships and carts from every shore meet at the Great Lake, and its guilds work in good order.

regional.name: Northern Shipwrights
regional.desc: The yards of the strait are old, and their masters know every plank of a hull.

regional.name: The Long Winters
regional.desc: The cold has made the folk hard and every building slow to raise.

regional.name: Western Freeholds
regional.desc: Free farmers and horse-breeders trade easily and send many sons to the muster.

regional.name: Charts of the Pupor Ocean
regional.desc: The islanders keep the oldest sea charts, and their fleets read the water well.

regional.name: Forge-Pits
regional.desc: The orc holds burn day and night, and the smiths ask few questions about the folk's needs.

regional.name: Elder Groves
regional.desc: Old lore lives in the groves, and craft and study go hand in hand.

regional.name: Furnace Lands
regional.desc: The Dead Lands are hot and storm-girt, and their war-forges never go cold.

regional.name: The Caravan Roads
regional.desc: Caravans carry the gold of the East to every court that will pay.

regional.name: Hospitable Isles
regional.desc: Poor in goods and rich in welcome, the isles keep a gentle peace.

regional.name: Sun-Blessed Fields
regional.desc: The fields of the Sunhot elves are ripe all year, and no one goes hungry.

timed.name: Full Granaries
timed.desc: The King's stores are full to the roof, and the builders work without fear of a hard year.

timed.name: Crown Debts
timed.desc: The treasury is bare and the creditors are at the gate.

timed.name: The Triumph
timed.desc: A great procession through Parim has lifted the people's hearts for a season.

timed.name: Western Tariffs Paid
timed.desc: The realm has paid the tariffs of the West, and its workshops make more for the folk to cover them.

timed.name: A Lean Year
timed.desc: The harvest was thin, and the folk have tightened their belts.

timed.name: The King's New Hall
timed.desc: A new hall in the Golden Court gives the courtiers something to admire.
